gloss: to escape; to get out; to break free

definitions.gloss: to escape; to get out; to break free
definitions.explanation: To get out of a dangerous, confined, or difficult situation. Used for physical escape from places as well as figurative escape from difficult circumstances.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}から{脱出|だっしゅつ}する。
{火事|かじ}のとき、{窓|まど}から{脱出|だっしゅつ}した。
examples.english: During the fire, I escaped through the window.

examples.japanese: {不況|ふきょう}から{脱出|だっしゅつ}するには{時間|じかん}がかかるだろう。
examples.english: It will probably take time to escape from the recession.

examples.japanese: {乗客|じょうきゃく}は{全員|ぜんいん}{無事|ぶじ}に{機内|きない}から{脱出|だっしゅつ}することができた。
examples.english: All passengers were able to escape from the aircraft safely.

notes:
Emphasizes getting out of a confined or dangerous space. Unlike {逃|に}げる which focuses on the act of running away, {脱出|だっしゅつ}する focuses on successfully getting free from entrapment or confinement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緊急|きんきゅう}{脱出|だっしゅつ}: emergency escape
- {脱出|だっしゅつ}{経路|けいろ}: escape route
- {脱出|だっしゅつ}ゲーム: escape room game
- {脱出|だっしゅつ}{速度|そくど}: escape velocity
- {危機|きき}からの{脱出|だっしゅつ}: escape from crisis

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {逃|に}げる: to flee — general running away from something
- {脱走|だっそう}する: to escape from custody — specifically breaking out of prison or military confinement
- {抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}す: to slip out — stealthily leaving a place without being noticed
